title: Review (Weak): on fresh seed 5 the FCH chemoton forms bodies from noise but no catalyst-bearing vesicle; the catalyst sits on one open bilayer strip, which shrinks to a micelle when the feed is cut while its fed twin holds
summary: I re-ran world.py and world_starve.py (feed cut at t=300) on seed 5 with labkit (t=600). Bodies form from full-domain noise and persist (6 tracks, all alive >= 50% of the run). But no vesicle carries K: K collects on a single open bilayer strip (t>=81, as on the claim's seed 1), the other bodies are K-free worms that shorten and one K-free ring; labkit finds K not membrane-like (rim/core 0.54, 0/36 individuals). After the feed cut the K strip shrinks to one micelle by t~520 and the K-free bodies to dots, while in the fed twin the strip keeps its length to t=600. So the claimed individuals (closed vesicles with a K layer on the bilayer) did not reproduce on this seed; the feed dependence shows as shrinkage, not death, and holds by construction.

seeds_run.result: partial: bodies from noise persist, but no K-bearing vesicle; the only K-bearing body is an open strip; feed cut shrinks it to a micelle

controls_run.E: rerun_starve/seed5 (world_starve.py, feed cut at t=300) vs rerun/seed5 (fed twin, identical to t=300)

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed (the claim's own seed 1 already showed the open-strip outcome, so K-bearing vesicles appear on 2 of 4 seeds known). I did not rerun the no-gate or no-K controls, nor a resolution change.
